paragraphs.title: A Request for Examination and a Declaration of Trust

easy.q: Whom does David ask to judge him?

easy.explanation: David says, “I have trusted also in the LORD.”
easy.q: In whom does David say he has trusted?

easy.explanation: David says, “I have walked in mine integrity.”

medium.explanation: David asks, “Examine me, O LORD, and prove me.”
medium.q: What does David ask the LORD to do in verse 2?

medium.explanation: Because David trusts in the LORD, he says, “therefore I shall not slide.”
medium.q: What does David connect with his trust in the LORD?

answers: He has lived according to God's truth
medium.explanation: David describes his life as guided by God's truth.
medium.q: What does the phrase “I have walked in thy truth” mean in this passage?

answers: He wants his inner thoughts and desires to be examined
He is asking for physical healing
He wants to hide his actions
challenge.explanation: The reins and heart represent a person's inward thoughts, motives, and desires.
challenge.q: Why does David ask the LORD to try his reins and his heart?

answers: The LORD's lovingkindness is before David's eyes and guides his truthful walk
Truth takes the place of God's lovingkindness
challenge.explanation: David says that God's lovingkindness is before his eyes while he walks in God's truth.
challenge.q: How are the LORD's lovingkindness and David's walk in truth connected?

answers: From God's house to deceitful people
From asking for judgment and examination to declaring trust and truth
challenge.explanation: David begins by asking to be judged and tested, then declares his trust and faithful walk.

paragraphs.title: Rejecting Wickedness and Approaching the Temple

easy.explanation: David says, “I have not sat with vain persons.”
easy.q: With whom does David say he has not sat?

easy.explanation: David says, “I have hated the congregation of evildoers.”
easy.q: Whom does David say he has hated?

easy.explanation: David says, “I have loved the habitation of thy house.”
easy.q: What does David say he has loved?

answers: Washing his hands and approaching God's altar
Stopping his worship of the LORD
medium.explanation: He says, “I will wash mine hands in innocency: so will I compass thine altar.”
medium.q: What does David describe after speaking about separating himself from evil people?

answers: People who serve at God's house
medium.explanation: The phrase describes people David refuses to join because they are empty, false, or worthless in character.
medium.q: What does “vain persons” most nearly mean in this context?

answers: To give thanks and tell of God's wondrous works
medium.explanation: David wants to proclaim thanksgiving and tell others about all God's wondrous works.
medium.q: Why does David want to publish with the voice of thanksgiving?

answers: Sitting with wicked people versus loving the habitation of God's house
challenge.explanation: David rejects fellowship with evildoers and chooses devotion to God's dwelling place.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast in this passage?

answers: It represents a desire for purity and integrity
It represents a desire for bribes
It represents a desire to avoid thanksgiving
challenge.explanation: The clean hands symbolize David's desire to approach God with purity and uprightness.
challenge.q: How does washing his hands in innocency relate to David's desire?

answers: Loving God's house, then turning away, then hatred
Rejecting evil, pursuing purity and thanksgiving, then loving God's house
Bribes, the altar, and then truthful people
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from avoiding evil people, to worship and thanksgiving, and finally to love for God's house.
challenge.q: What sequence of ideas appears in verses 4–8?

paragraphs.title: A Plea to Be Separated from the Fate of Sinners

easy.explanation: David asks, “Gather not my soul with sinners, nor my life with bloody men.”
easy.q: With whom does David ask not to have his soul gathered?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “their right hand is full of bribes.”
easy.q: What is full in the right hand of the wicked?

easy.explanation: The verse says that in their hands is “mischief.”
easy.q: What is in the hands of the bloody men?

answers: To be separated from sinners and their fate
medium.explanation: David asks not to be gathered together with sinners and bloody men.
medium.q: What is David's main request in these verses?

answers: An evil deed or harmful scheme
medium.explanation: Here, “mischief” refers to wrongdoing or harmful plans.
medium.q: What does “mischief” mean in this context?

answers: As people whose hearts are full of truth
As people whose hands hold evil and whose right hands are full of bribes
medium.explanation: They are characterized by mischief and bribery.
medium.q: How does the passage describe the bloody men?

answers: He wants separation because they are associated with mischief and bribes
He wants separation because they love God's house
He wants separation because they give thanks
challenge.explanation: Their evil actions and corruption explain why David does not want to share their fate.
challenge.q: How does the description of the wicked explain David's request to be separated from them?

challenge.explanation: The parallel words show that David asks for complete separation from the sinners.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the words “my soul” and “my life” together?

answers: From loving God's habitation to asking not to be gathered with wicked people
From walking in integrity to sitting with evildoers
challenge.explanation: After expressing love for God's house, David asks to be kept apart from sinners and corrupt men.
challenge.q: What change of thought occurs between verses 8 and 10?

paragraphs.title: Walking in Innocence and Belonging to the Righteous

easy.explanation: David says, “I will walk in mine integrity.”
easy.q: How does David say he will walk?

easy.explanation: He asks, “redeem me, and be merciful unto me.”
easy.q: What does David ask for after declaring his integrity?

easy.explanation: David says, “My foot standeth in an even place.”
easy.q: Where does David say his foot stands?

medium.explanation: David asks the LORD to redeem him and be merciful unto him.
medium.q: What does David ask of the LORD in response to his walk in integrity?

medium.explanation: An even place suggests stability, uprightness, and a straight way.
medium.q: What does “an even place” suggest in this passage?

medium.explanation: David concludes, “in the congregations will I bless the LORD.”
medium.q: What does David say he will do in the congregations?

answers: Both describe a straight and stable way of life
Both describe fellowship with bloody men
Both express a desire for bribes
challenge.explanation: Integrity and an even place together picture moral uprightness and stability.
challenge.q: How is standing in an even place related to walking in integrity?

answers: He asks for mercy and hopes to continue worshiping God among the congregation
He asks to withdraw from every congregation
He asks to join the bloody men
challenge.explanation: David seeks redemption and mercy so that he may remain among God's worshiping people.
challenge.q: How are David's request for mercy and his blessing of the LORD connected?

answers: David wants to continue in integrity and bless the LORD among the congregation
David wants to return to the congregation of evildoers
David gives up his trust in the LORD
challenge.explanation: The final verses summarize integrity, a request for redemption and mercy, and public blessing of the LORD.
